analysis.session_summary: The session was dominated by a broad yen bid and CHF selloff: JPY added 0.501% while CHF lost -0.413%, with CHF/JPY down -150.9 pips and USD/CHF up +48.4 pips. GBP was the other outperformer, up 0.268% after UK GDP beat 0.4% vs 0.0%, though GBP/USD netted only +0.6 pips. USD strength was selective: DXY gained +22.5 points to 99.051, and EUR/USD fell -39.1 pips to 1.15655, but USD/JPY fell -32.0 pips. Key US events—Core CPI at 0.3% vs 0.2% and UoM 47.8 vs 51.0—printed muted currency basket impulses of 0.008% and 0.029%, leaving the tape more flow-driven than data-driven.

themes.evidence: JPY mean +0.501% vs major peers vs CHF -0.413%; CHF/JPY dropped -150.9 pips; USD/CHF rose +48.4 pips; USD/JPY fell -32.0 pips.
GBP second strongest at +0.268%; UK GDP m/m actual 0.4% vs forecast 0.0% produced normal GBP impulse +0.075%; EUR/GBP fell -29.4 pips; GBP/USD held +0.6 pips despite USD strength.

themes.theme: Selective USD strength; US data muted
themes.evidence: USD +0.263%; DXY +22.5 points; USD/CHF +48.4 and USD/CAD +34.3 but USD/JPY -32.0 and EUR/USD -39.1; Core CPI basket impulse 0.008% and UoM 0.029% both inside the noise floor.
NZD weakest at -0.57%; NZD/USD -42.4 pips with close at 0.05 of its 53.5 range; AUD/NZD +72.5 pips; no leg had a clear catalyst.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD printed down legs of -17.7 and -48.4 pips around a +22.7 pip rebound, closing -39.1 pips at 1.15655 in the bottom 0.06 of its 52.9-pip range with no clear catalyst for any leg.
leg_notes.USD/JPY: USD/JPY whipsawed through eight legs; the largest -89.0 pip decline had CPI contributing -24.1 pips (27%), while a +30.3 pip UoM-related bounce was medium confidence, leaving the pair -32.0 pips at 154.024.
leg_notes.GBP/USD: GBP/USD rose +17.6 pips on UK GDP (contributing +12.7 pips, 72% of the leg), then gave back -28.6 pips on UoM, netting +0.6 pips at 1.35033.
leg_notes.AUD/USD: AUD/USD's +20.4 pip initial rise was erased by a -42.2 pip decline before a +7.6 pip bounce, closing -10.0 pips at 0.71507 with no clear catalysts.
leg_notes.NZD/USD: NZD/USD lost -49.6 pips in its main down-leg after a +4.7 pip open, closing -42.4 pips at 0.5784, the weakest major at -0.57%.
leg_notes.USD/CHF: USD/CHF shook off a -3.5 pip dip to rally +56.1 pips, closing +48.4 pips at 0.81823 at the 0.97 percentile of its 59.5-pip range.
leg_notes.USD/CAD: USD/CAD climbed +42.8 pips and retraced only -6.3 pips, closing +34.3 pips at 1.38744, consistent with firm USD.
leg_notes.EUR/CHF: EUR/CHF chopped higher in five small legs, including a +26.1 pip up-leg, ending +24.2 pips at 0.94631 despite muted euro impulses.
leg_notes.CHF/JPY: CHF/JPY collapsed -195.1 pips in one leg with Core CPI contributing -39.2 pips (20%), then rebounded +53.9 pips, closing -150.9 pips at 188.232.
leg_notes.AUD/NZD: AUD/NZD advanced in five choppy legs—largest +57.3 and -30.9—to close +72.5 pips at 1.23618 near 0.96 of its 80.0-pip range.
leg_notes.EUR/GBP: EUR/GBP fell in a single -30.0 pip leg over 4,305 minutes, with UK GDP contributing -5.8 pips (19%), closing -29.4 pips at 0.85646.
leg_notes.AUD/CHF: AUD/CHF rose in two up-legs of +33.5 and +13.1 around a -20.5 dip, closing +26.2 pips at 0.58506.
leg_notes.NZD/CHF: NZD/CHF see-sawed through six small legs of at most ±19.0 pips, closing -6.5 pips at 0.47325 with no clear catalyst.
leg_notes.USD/SEK: USD/SEK reversed a -1,352.6 pip drop with a +1,837.3 pip surge, closing +446.5 pips at 9.73378 after a 1.924% up-leg.
leg_notes.USD/NOK: USD/NOK swung from +325.7 to -707.6 to +597.0 pips, closing +216.3 pips at 9.30468.
leg_notes.USD/ZAR: USD/ZAR fell -747.0 pips then rallied +790.0 pips, closing -86.7 pips at 16.1792; UoM contributed +193.8 pips (25%) to the up-leg.
leg_notes.USD/MXN: USD/MXN chopped through six legs, including a Core CPI-linked -401.8 pip slide and UoM-linked +411.5 pip rebound, closing +153.8 pips at 16.99801.
leg_notes.Brent/USD: Brent/USD whipsawed through -284.9, +180.9, -275.3, and +477.3 pip legs, netting -9.1 pips at 109.153 with no single catalyst.

polarity_reads.read: Own-ccy impulse 0.008% was inside the noise floor despite a 0.3% vs 0.2% beat; top movers were USD/MXN +214.9 pips and USD/ZAR +312.3 pips, so the dollar did not get a broad bid—the reaction was concentrated in high-beta EM, suggesting positioning rather than a rates shock.
UK monthly GDP beat 0.4% vs 0.0% produced a normal GBP-strength impulse of 0.075%; EUR/GBP fell -2.4 pips and GBP/USD rose +3.7 pips, confirming GBP is trading on UK growth data.

The 47.8 vs 51.0 miss generated only a 0.029% basket impulse—inside noise; USD/MXN +122 pips and USD/ZAR +174.8 pips were outliers, implying soft US consumer data is not broadly weakening the dollar here.
Both Lagarde appearances were muted (0.018% and 0.000% own-ccy impulse), so euro policy remarks did not drive EUR crosses; EUR/CHF and EUR/GBP moved on other currencies.
The speech produced a -0.013% basket impulse inside noise, so the CHF weakness (-0.413%) was not driven by SNB communication but by broader flow or rate differentials.

scenarios.name: Risk-off / volatility spike
scenarios.thesis: Geopolitical headlines around Iran/Saudi are present and Brent had a +477.3 pip up-leg; a renewed Mideast escalation could force flight to safety, reversing CHF weakness and extending JPY strength while high-beta currencies suffer.

pair_paths.rationale: USD/JPY's session range is 123.5 pips and it closed -32.0 at 154.024; risk-off could resume the CPI-driven -89.0 pip leg.
USD/CHF near 0.81823 top of its 59.5 range; risk-off would unwind the +48.4 pip gain.
NZD/USD already -42.4 pips with a 53.5 range; risk-off could push to fresh lows.

risks.why_it_matters: The window spans weekend and Asia reopen; many legs had no clear catalyst and were flow-driven, making sharp gaps possible in USD/JPY and USD/CHF.
Brent whipsawed from -275.3 to +477.3 pips and headlines included Iran/Saudi items; a headline shock can quickly reverse risk sentiment despite VIX down -20.4 points.
Core CPI and UoM each moved baskets under noise (0.008% and 0.029%), so upcoming US prints may not produce textbook USD direction; positioning and risk channels dominate.
CHF is weakest at -0.413% and USD/CHF closed near the top at 0.97 of its range; a sentiment shift could force a sharp USD/CHF downside reversal within its 59.5-pip range.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: CAD CPI at 14:30 is the main event: m/m forecast -0.1% vs previous 0.5%, while median and trimmed y/y are seen at 2.0% and 1.9%; a downside surprise could weaken CAD and push USD/CAD above its 1.38744 close. ECB President Lagarde speaks at 17:15, but two prior Lagarde speeches were muted, so EUR impact is likely limited. No US high-impact data is scheduled in this window.
